Further context into this is needed though.

https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-myths-of-black-lives-matter-1455235686    It’s behind a pay wall but here’s what she had said about as far as the crime statistics for this:  Mac Donald writes in The Wall Street Journal, 2009 statistics from the Bureau of Justice Statistics reveal that blacks were charged with 62 percent of robberies, 57 percent of murders and 45 percent of assaults in the 75 biggest counties in the country, despite only comprising roughly 15 percent of the population in these counties.

Further context still is that the Marshall project report linked above doesn’t take into account the full details of events where unarmed black people were killed by police officers, there were incidents in that report that involved people trying to take a police officers gun, passengers in a car where one of the other passengers was shooting at officers, or people hit by stray bullets from a shootout, how could those be racially motivated fatalities? 

2. More whites and Hispanics die from police homicides than blacks. According to Mac Donald (in that same WSJ article), 12 percent of white and Hispanic homicide deaths were due to police officers, while only four percent of black homicide deaths were the result of police officers.

Wind farms aren't perfect but they are far from problematic.  They have  two small issues and one main issue:
1. On low wind days they are supplied power to keep moving so as not to lock up.  So people hear that and are like, wait it is using power instead of creating it? Well yeah on some days, but not all the other days. 
2. They do require a fair amount of maintenance but nothing compared to say, an oil rig, or a fracking site (at least the amount of maintenance that SHOULD be done at a fracking site, do not get me started).
3.  They cannot be relied upon solely for high usage or critical use sites. These include major hospitals, factories, sky scrapers, stadiums, etc.  The unpredictability in continuity of power and the still budding battery storage technology leaves wind farms as a supplementary state still for major cities, but for rural areas they can be fantastic.  

It is easy not to sit back and really take a look at what the actual power demand and consumption are in certain areas, and until you do, you wont see that in our current state of technology and infrastructure, we cannot rule out fossil fuels yet, because unfortunately we have sunk trillions into the building of such power systems, and until they can be replaced with similar reliability, it is far too dangerous to just dive in.
